analysis: Both changed files are documentation only. docs/developer/test.md changes the date stamp and adds descriptions of the NemotronSuperOpenRouterVideoTests (head lines 1073-1077) and NemotronSuperOpenRouterCapabilityTests (lines 1097-1104) suites. The doc says these are CPU-only or tiny-fixture tests that load no model weights, and they add no secrets, credentials, or production endpoints. docs/provider/direct-mode.md changes the date stamp and edits table rows for the local Nemotron endpoint. These now cover response_format combined with tools, and the media request-body limit moved from 8 MiB to a 413 at `localInferenceMaxUploadBytes`, with the owner's own 40 MiB bound (`NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes`) sitting above it. The 40 MiB bound versus the chat route limit is a documentation claim about unchanged code. This diff does not show the code, so I cannot confirm the doc matches the implementation, and the doc claims a 413 is returned before decoding. No source code, auth, attestation, encryption, or cache-storage behavior changed (T-041, TB-007 and TB-011 are unaffected). The threat model's own T-041 content was not touched by the diff. The remaining question for integration is whether the documented upload-limit semantics match the actual code. That is documentation accuracy rather than a verified security regression. No findings.
